/-! Raw squared-variable numerator coefficients for Evans--Veselov--Winn 6.3.
The outer polynomial variable is u=x², the inner one v=y²; w=z² is set to 1.
Homogeneity recovers its exponent a+b-1-i-j. No factorial normalization.
-/
namespace MathGKM.Markov

noncomputable section

abbrev BiPoly := Polynomial (Polynomial ℤ)
def U : BiPoly := Polynomial.X
def V : BiPoly := Polynomial.C Polynomial.X
def S : BiPoly := U + V + 1
def coeff (P : BiPoly) (i j : ℕ) : ℤ := (P.coeff i).coeff j

structure Label where
  a : ℕ
  b : ℕ
  p : BiPoly

structure Frame where
  lo : Label
  mid : Label
  hi : Label

def initial : Frame :=
  ⟨⟨0, 1, 1⟩, ⟨1, 2, (U + V)^2 + U⟩, ⟨1, 1, U + V⟩⟩

def advance (f : Frame) (right : Bool) : Frame :=
  if right then
    ⟨f.mid, ⟨f.mid.a + f.hi.a, f.mid.b + f.hi.b,
      S * f.hi.p * f.mid.p - U^f.hi.a * V^f.hi.b * f.lo.p⟩, f.hi⟩
  else
    ⟨f.lo, ⟨f.lo.a + f.mid.a, f.lo.b + f.mid.b,
      S * f.lo.p * f.mid.p - U^f.lo.a * V^f.lo.b * f.hi.p⟩, f.mid⟩

def frame (path : List Bool) : Frame := path.foldl advance initial

def InPolygon (a b i j : ℕ) : Prop :=
  a * b ≤ b * i + a * j ∧ i + j ≤ a + b - 1

def WeakLC (a b : ℕ) (P : BiPoly) : Prop :=
  (∀ i j, InPolygon a b i j → InPolygon a b (i+1) j →
    InPolygon a b (i+2) j →
    coeff P i j * coeff P (i+2) j ≤ coeff P (i+1) j ^ 2) ∧
  (∀ i j, InPolygon a b i j → InPolygon a b i (j+1) →
    InPolygon a b i (j+2) →
    coeff P i j * coeff P i (j+2) ≤ coeff P i (j+1) ^ 2) ∧
  (∀ i j, InPolygon a b i (j+2) → InPolygon a b (i+1) (j+1) →
    InPolygon a b (i+2) j →
    coeff P i (j+2) * coeff P (i+2) j ≤ coeff P (i+1) (j+1) ^ 2)

/-- Full path-indexed target, not asserted as a theorem. The initial endpoint
0/1 has P=1 and a singleton polygon; 1/1 has P=u+v. -/
def Conjecture63 : Prop :=
  WeakLC 0 1 1 ∧ WeakLC 1 1 (U+V) ∧
  ∀ path, let m := (frame path).mid; WeakLC m.a m.b m.p

end
end MathGKM.Markov

# Second horizontal row

Machine-authored research, 2026-10-14; request 8934af1772f94a59862d7005ebd43159.
Full Conjecture 6.3 remains open. This is not an independent completion audit.

For an arbitrary word A w B, let n=length(w), m=count_B(w). When w is
nonempty, let f and r indicate that its first and last letters are B, and
let k count adjacent BB pairs inside w. Put s=f+r+2k. The exact formula for
n>=3 is

    2 [v²]P = u^m (1+u)^(n-3) Q(u),
    Q(u) = 4s + (9m²+13m+6)u
         + (6m²+6mn+8m+6n+6)u²
         + (m+n+2)(m+n+1)u³.

There is also a denominator-cleared identity valid for every nonempty core:
multiply the second coefficient by 2(1+u)^3 and the cubic by u^m(1+u)^n.
The formula is proved by a second-order coefficient invariant of the literal
positive matrix recurrence, over arbitrary commutative rings. In particular,
the order-dependent constant is not replaced by a conjectured count formula.
An induction proves 0<=s<=2m.

For actual source words, a=m+1 and b=n+2. If n>2m, the exponent (m,2)
lies below the source polygon. The inherited support theorem therefore makes
its raw coefficient zero. Extracting coefficient m from the displayed formula
forces s=0. This uses an actual source theorem, not an assumed balanced-word
identification. If n<=2m, the elementary bound s<=2m suffices instead.

Write the cubic coefficients as A,B,C,D. The polynomial certificates establish
A,C,B,D>=0, AC<=B², BD<=C² and AD<=BC for m<=n and
(n<=2m or s=0). They yield the zero-extended CrossLC property of Q. The already
checked binomial smoothing and shift adapters yield CrossLC of the literal
source row. Seven core words of length at most two are evaluated separately;
their rows are shifted nonnegative quadratics with checked coefficient gaps.
The final target theorem is horizontal_two_raw8934, in
research/MarkovSecondHorizontal8934.lean. Consult the validation manifest for
actual accepted build/replay status, rather than treating this prose as a receipt.

This argument does not establish the stronger arbitrary-word horizontal
conjecture. The cubic before binomial smoothing can fail LC for long words
with B at a core endpoint, so merely applying residual LC to every word would
be unjustified. General higher horizontal rows remain open here.

## Experiments and searches

matrix-invariants.json records 1,023 products beginning with A through length
10. All four entries passed the horizontal adjacent checks. Three simple
same-row synchronization predicates failed, so that induction route was not
used. This is finite evidence only, not a proof of horizontal LC.

polygon-words-14.json records 8,191 A--core--B words through length 14. Of
these, 253 have their entire coefficient support in the polygon specified by
their counts; 63 of those have coprime counts. No directional LC failure was
found among the 253. No family-identification or universal theorem follows
from this scan. Earlier arbitrary-word failures do not automatically survive
this stronger support requirement.

Hosted searches on 2026-10-14 retrieved these primary sources:

* [Evans–Veselov–Winn, published target](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/Articles/250708-Winn/index.html):
  exact target and known special-line results; no general proof retrieved.
* [Evans, Saturation of Markov Polynomials](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18333):
  the abstract reports a constructive saturation proof using snake graphs.
  Saturation is distinct from the raw log-concavity inequalities.
* [Kang–Lee–Lim, Unimodality and Cluster Algebras from Surfaces](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.04396):
  the abstract reports unimodality and states a log-concavity conjecture for a
  different specialization. No theorem from this paper was imported into Lean.

The search supplied no universal proof of this pinned root. No historical
novelty claim is made for the second-row identity or inequality.

second-formula-check.json verifies the exact second-row formula on 2,040
words of lengths 5 through 12. It also records the non-source word A B A^16 B
with coprime counts 2/19: its residual is [0,2,14,112,190], so 196<224.
The actual source word is different; this is not a root refutation.
# Positive support and failed stronger inequalities

Machine-authored request 7252232b; full Conjecture63 remains open.

For an arbitrary Boolean core word w, put f_empty=g_empty=1. Prepending a
letter replaces (f,g) by (h+f,h) for true, and (h,h+g) for false, where
h=v*f+u*g. These polynomials are exactly the two components of the inherited
gas matrix product applied to the terminal column (1,u). The scalar partition
function is h. This is an exact positive recurrence, not a change of raw
coefficient normalization.

At word length n, both f and g have a positive coefficient at every degree-n
monomial. Moreover, a positive coefficient at (i,j) stays positive at every
(k,l) with k>=i, l>=j and k+l<=n. The induction uses positivity of sums and
shifts. Adding the lower-degree f or g is safe at degrees <=n by induction;
at degree n+1 positivity comes from the full top of h. The proof does not
assume that sums preserve log-concavity.

MarkovSupport725 proves these assertions and connects h to every exact source
numerator through source_gas80, with n+1=a+b-1. Hence every source coefficient
propagates northeast to the top degree. MarkovIntervals725 combines this with
the checked outside-polygon-zero theorem: every horizontal and vertical row
has interval positive support, including its zero extension to integers.
Consequently adjacent raw LC and CrossLC are equivalent for these two source
directions, with no additional no-gap hypothesis. Neither LC side is proved
by this equivalence.

## Quotient slices and the residual audit

The inherited rowStep774, with x the inner variable and t the outer variable,
has the same positive recurrence with h=f+x*t*g and an added t*f or t*g.
MarkovResidualSupport725 proves simultaneously that each row r has positive
support extending from any positive coefficient to index r, that the outer
degree is bounded by the word length, and that every diagonal coefficient
(r,r) within that length is positive. A separate wedge invariant proves
coefficients vanish when the inner index exceeds the outer index.

The exact source_word774 bridge identifies these polynomials with the actual
quotientSlice774, retaining letter order. Thus every quotient slice has
interval positive support. Its top coefficient at index r is positive for
r<b, and the whole slice is zero for r>=b. No finite path or denominator
bound enters this proof. The conditional upper-raw transfer now requires only
the adjacent residual LC inequalities, with the former interval-support
premise discharged. This addresses the specific zero-gap issue in the
independent residual audit. It does not prove those residual inequalities,
and cancellation in the lower-half factorization still gives no LC theorem.

Finite exact probes rejected two possible stronger inequalities. Coefficientwise
LC in the remaining variable fails at the actual word ABB (2/3). Factorial-
weighted horizontal LC fails at source 21/22, at j=24, i=0,1,2, where the raw
coefficients are 190,13965,514845. The reversed stronger inequality is
13965^2 < 2*190*514845; the raw inequality 190*514845 <= 13965^2 holds.
MarkovFactorialObstruction725 separately proves the exact 21/22 coefficients,
all three polygon memberships, the reversed factorial-weighted inequality,
and the valid raw inequality. This is a strategy obstruction, not a root
refutation. The other probes remain finite experimental evidence only.

/-- Cross inequalities include ordinary adjacent log-concavity, and keep zeros. -/
def CrossLC (f : ℤ → ℝ) : Prop :=

def Smooth (f : ℤ → ℝ) (k : ℤ) : ℝ := f k + f (k-1)

theorem crossLC_shift {f : ℤ → ℝ} (h : CrossLC f) (s : ℤ) :
    CrossLC (fun k => f (k+s)) := by

theorem crossLC_forward {f : ℤ → ℝ} (h : CrossLC f) :
    CrossLC (fun k => f k + f (k+1)) := by

  have h1 := h i j hij
  have h2 := h (i+1) (j+1) (by omega)
  have h3 := h i (j+1) (by omega)
  have h4 := h (i+1) j (by omega)
  dsimp only
  nlinarith

theorem crossLC_smooth {f : ℤ → ℝ} (h : CrossLC f) : CrossLC (Smooth f) := by
  have hs := crossLC_shift (crossLC_forward h) (-1)

## Palindrome and positive squares

Let W be the exact A/B source word. The two word substitutions are
L(A)=A,L(B)=AB and R(A)=AB,R(B)=B. Naturality with the actual Farey pair
recursion proves W=A c B where c is the recursively defined central word.
If c is a palindrome, L(c)A and B R(c) are palindromes; induction proves this
for every finite source path. Expanding B to AC gives the exact gas core
L(c)A, again a palindrome. This is an exact source-word assertion, stronger
than merely exhibiting an unspecified word with the right counts.

For a gas word w with matrix M, define

    Q_w(x,y)=v*x²*M.a+u*v*x*y*M.b+x*y*M.c+u*y²*M.d.

Sandwiching w by the same letter transforms its boundary pair by

    h=v*x+u*y,
    (x,y) -> (h+t*x,h) for C, or (h,h+t*y) for A.

The empty core has Q=v*x²+u*y². A singleton has
Q=(v*x+u*y)²+t*v*x² for C, or Q=(v*x+u*y)²+t*u*y² for A.
These are polynomial identities over arbitrary commutative rings.
At t=1, palindrome induction and nonnegativity of all boundary updates prove
that every actual source raw numerator has one of these three forms:

    v*f²+u*g²,  f²+u*g²,  f²+v*g²,

where f,g are bivariate integer polynomials with nonnegative coefficients.
MarkovSquares28b1.source_positive_squares28 states exactly this existential
result. No log-concavity closure under addition or squaring is invoked.

The exact Python check agrees with all 627 source polynomials through b=45.
It also finds that the canonical half polynomial f can fail raw vertical LC:
at source 3/44 it has [12,14,18], so 196<216. This is an experimental
obstruction to requiring LC of every half factor; it is not a counterexample
to the source numerator, and this obstruction has not been formalized in Lean.

## Lower support determines the canonical word

For arbitrary positive raw matrix words the following monomials have strictly
positive coefficients. Write B-count as c and word length as l:

* In x r y: u^(c(y)) v^(l(x)+indicator(r=B)).
* In A x r y B: u^(c(x)+1) v^(l(y)+2).

The first path stays in the upper matrix state, exits at r, then stays in
the lower state. The second exits at the initial A, returns at r, and exits
again at the final B. MarkovWordWitness28b1 proves positivity directly from
the exact raw generators and coefficient convolution, not by tropical tests.

Let w=A x r y B have a B letters and length b, with 0<a<b and gcd(a,b)=1.
Suppose every positive coefficient satisfies a*b<=b*i+a*j. Put k=c(x),
l=l(x)+1. The suffix witness yields b*k<=a*l; the prefix-loop witness yields
a*l<=b*(k+1). Equality in the latter would force b|l by coprimality, impossible
for 0<l<b. Therefore k=floor(a*l/b). All proper prefix counts are forced.
The full core count is a-1, which also determines its final letter.

MarkovPolygonWord28b1 formalizes the floor constraint. MarkovWordRigidity28b1
uses equality of all prefix counts to prove uniqueness of a supported core.

every such reduced A--core--B word with an actual source path and its literal

and raw GlobalLC for every reduced A--core--B word satisfying the lower

These results provide global structural descriptions of the exact source

## Exact all-source change of exponents

Set u=x, v=xy. For the source a/b let c be its inherited exact central A/B
word (length b-2, B-count a-1). The new denominator-free gauge calculation
proves

    P_(a/b)(x,xy) = x^a F_c(x,y),
    F_c = (y,1) T_c (x(1+y), 1+x(1+y))^T,
    T_A = [[xy,x],[xy,1+x]],
    T_B = [[y+xy(1+y),x(1+y)],
           [2y+xy(1+y),1+x(1+y)]] .

Both transfers are linear in x with nonnegative coefficients. Their linear
parts are H and (1+y)H, where H=[[y,1],[y,1]] and H^2=(1+y)H.
The constant parts are D_A=[[0,0],[0,1]] and D_B=[[y,0],[2y,1]].
This is an exact polynomial identity at x=0 as well: the proof multiplies
through the diagonal gauge and cancels only the nonzero polynomial X, never
a real value or a raw coefficient.

For s=i+j-a >=0 the literal coefficient identity is

    A(i,j) = [x^s y^j] F_c.

With i,j natural and i+j=a+s, the polygon condition is exactly

    s <= b-1,  (b-a)j <= b s.

The natural original index also retains j<=a+s. The three original
directions become respectively (1,0), (1,1), and (0,1) in (s,j). In
particular, a horizontal-only argument in these new variables does NOT
establish the original vertical or diagonal clauses.

## A broader sufficient horizontal target

For an arbitrary A/B word w let N=length(w)+1 and C_w(s,j)=[x^s y^j]F_w.
The proposed assertion is

    (s+2)(N-s) C_w(s,j) C_w(s+2,j)
       <= (s+1)(N-s-1) C_w(s+1,j)^2,   s+2<=N.

The new reduction connects this explicitly unproved all-word assertion to
the actual source ambient bound and hence raw horizontal inequalities.
It does not assume arbitrary-word vertical or diagonal log-concavity.

The exact enumeration extends earlier no-adjacent-C experiments to the
ambient bound: 28,656 gas cores of length 1 through 21, beginning and ending
in A and with no CC, give 4,415,699 nontrivial horizontal triples without
failure. Every such core is expand(w)A for a unique original A/B word w.
Zero endpoint products are omitted only from the nontrivial count; they
satisfy the tested inequality because all coefficients and both scalar
weights in range are nonnegative. This is finite evidence, not a proof.

## Exact Pell generating kernel

For c=B^(a-1), write Q_a=F_c and Q_0=1. The new formal recurrence is

    Q_1=1+x(1+y)^2,
    Q_(a+2)=(1+y+x(1+y)^2)Q_(a+1)-y Q_a.

As an ordinary formal power series in z, it gives the checked equation

    [(1-z)(1-yz)-xz(1+y)^2] sum_(a>=0) Q_a z^a = 1-yz.

The exact source coefficient bridge retains every natural i,j,s satisfying
i+j=a+s. This supplies the source interpretation of the ambient kernel.
The recurrence also gives the checked Cassini identity

    Q_a Q_(a+2)-Q_(a+1)^2 = x y^(a+1)(1+y)^2.

Its sign concerns the FAMILY index a, not any pinned coefficient direction.
It must not be used as a coefficient log-concavity assertion.

Writing K_s(z)=sum_(a>=0) [x^s]Q_a z^a, the extracted recurrence is

    (1-z)(1-yz) K_(s+1) = z(1+y)^2 K_s,
    (1-z) K_0 = 1.

MarkovAmbientSlices5c90 proves these equations over every commutative ring,
then proves by induction the denominator-cleared form of

    sum_(a>=s) [x^s]Q_a z^a
      = z^s(1+y)^(2s)/[(1-z)^(s+1)(1-yz)^s].

The extracted identity is therefore checked as an ordinary formal-power-series
equation, including s=0, with no division or convergence assumption. Its
positive binomial expansion is compatible with the inherited exact binomial
sums. None of these identities proves the aggregate coefficient inequality;
global horizontal aggregation remains open.

For c=A (actual source 1/3), the new exact identity is

The exact source identity and strict positivity are proved in Lean; the
Sturm probe independently records zero real roots. This rules out blanket

ambient coefficient bound or the published raw inequalities. In particular,

Both are nonnegative on their stated support. Vanishing endpoints are handled
separately, so no division by a zero coefficient is involved.

For B, exact binomial recurrences give

    (s+1) B_q(s) B_(q+1)(s+2)
      <= (s+2) B_q(s+1) B_(q+1)(s+1),
    (s+1) B_(q+1)(s) B_q(s+2)
      = s B_(q+1)(s+1) B_q(s+1).

The first cleared difference is 2q times a nonnegative binomial product.
Multiplying the appropriate B and C comparisons cancels their positive
scalar factors. Multiplication with the A comparison proves the claim.
The fractions used during proof are only algebraic certificates; the final
inequalities compare the unchanged integer summands.

## Consequences and remaining gap

Any fixed two consecutive charge classes form a coefficientwise log-concave
sequence of polynomials in the charge variable. The outer two gap coefficients
use inherited individual-summand LC; the middle coefficient uses the new
mixed inequality. Every polynomial coefficient, including zeros, is retained.

For the full refined horizontal polynomial, the coefficient of charge one
in its LC gap is nonnegative for every parameter. It has just the two
ordered products of charge indices 0 and 1. Coefficients of larger total
charge contain more widely separated pairs and remain unresolved.
This theorem does not prove evaluation at source weight one is nonnegative.
